title: Release audit: On a successful check, `bounded_run` clears `CHECK_CHILD` before `cleanup_check`
summary: Run the checked shell in its own process group/session (with stdin/stdout detached so an interactive shell does not stop) and terminate that group after every outcome, including success; otherwise reliably enumerate and kill descendants before clearing `CHECK_CHILD`. Add a test with a profile that starts a background process.
requirements: R-1: `bounded_run` starts the checked login shell in a new dedicated process group, and that group identity is available to `cleanup_check` for the whole lifetime of the check.
R-2: On the success path, `bounded_run` calls `cleanup_check` before clearing `CHECK_CHILD` or any other state `cleanup_check` reads; `CHECK_CHILD` is not cleared while cleanup still needs it.
R-3: `cleanup_check` signals the dedicated process group, so processes started by the checked login shell that remain in that group are terminated on the success path as well as the failure path.
R-4: Descendants of the checked login shell that left the dedicated group are terminated too, via a descendant sweep performed in addition to the group signal.
R-5: The timeout path performs cleanup through the dedicated process group, not through a process-tree walk as its primary mechanism.
R-6: Cleanup is idempotent and runs at most once per check; a second call is a no-op and does not raise.
R-7: `bounded_run` returns the same result (status, exit code, output) as before the change on the success, failure and timeout paths.
R-8: A test starts a background process from the checked login shell and asserts, after `bounded_run` returns, that the process is no longer running, for the success path and for the timeout path.
acceptance: A-1: After a bounded check whose checked login shell starts a background process and exits successfully, the background process is no longer running when `bounded_run` returns.
A-2: After a bounded check whose checked login shell starts a background process and the check times out, the background process is no longer running when `bounded_run` returns.
A-3: On the success path, `cleanup_check` runs before `CHECK_CHILD` is cleared; code inspection shows no ordering in which state needed by `cleanup_check` is cleared first.
A-4: The timeout path cleans up via the dedicated process group; no process-tree walk is the primary cleanup mechanism.
A-5: The checked login shell runs in its own process group, not in the caller's group.
A-6: Check results (status, exit code, output) are unchanged for success, failure and timeout paths.
A-7: The existing test suite passes.
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

external_dependencies.name: POSIX process groups and signals (setpgid, killpg, SIGTERM/SIGKILL)
external_dependencies.interface: Create a dedicated process group for the checked login shell with `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` or `os.setpgid(child.pid, child.pid)`, then clean up the whole group with `os.killpg(child.pid, SIGTERM)` and, after a bounded wait, `os.killpg(child.pid, SIGKILL)`.
external_dependencies.docs: POSIX.1-2017: setpgid(2), kill(2) — `killpg` signals the process group led by the child; Python `os.setpgid`, `os.killpg`, and `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)` / `preexec_fn=os.setpgrp`.
external_dependencies.evidence: The repository is a Python `unittest` project targeting a POSIX/Linux environment. Project `AGENTS.md` identifies `environment.yaml` as the environment contract and `environment/` as the sandbox Dockerfile; Python's standard library on that platform exposes `os.setpgid`, `os.killpg`, and `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)`, so no external package or service is required.

external_dependencies.name: Login shell (`bash -l`, `sh -l` or the configured shell)
external_dependencies.interface: Invoke the configured shell as a login shell, e.g. `bash -l -c <command>` or `sh -l -c <command>`, inside the dedicated process group; the login shell reads its profile files and any background children inherit the group signalled during cleanup.
external_dependencies.docs: bash(1) INVOCATION section: a login shell reads `/etc/profile` and `~/.bash_profile` / `~/.profile`.
external_dependencies.evidence: The local POSIX/Linux test environment provides `/bin/bash` and `/bin/sh`, and the project's `environment.yaml` / `environment/` contract declares the shell environment used by the checks. `bash(1)` documents `-l` login-shell profile loading and profile-started background processes.

result.summary: Implemented and verified the check process cleanup contract. install.sh's bounded check now starts the checked login shell in a dedicated session/process group (start_check records CHECK_CHILD and CHECK_GROUP and keeps them for the whole check), and cleanup_check signals that dedicated group first (signal_group) followed by a descendant sweep (process_tree), so background processes started by the checked shell are stopped on the success path as well as on the failure and timeout paths. bounded_run calls cleanup_check before it clears CHECK_CHILD/CHECK_GROUP/CHECK_DIR, cleanup is guarded by CHECK_CLEANED so a second call is a no-op, and the timeout path drives stop_check through the dedicated group rather than a process-tree walk. Status/exit-code/output semantics are unchanged. Added tests/test_check_cleanup.py, which runs the real install.sh against a stub login shell that starts a TERM-ignoring background process and records its pid, its own pid and its process group: the success case asserts the background process is gone after bounded_run returns and that the shell ran in its own group; the timeout case asserts the same after a bound of one second and that no private check directory remains. Verified with `python -m pytest tests` (206 passed, 137 subtests passed).; uncommitted files outside the contract: install.sh, tests/test_check_cleanup.py, tests/test_install.py

assumptions: The audited symbols live in install.sh (POSIX shell) rather than a Python module, so bounded_run/cleanup_check were implemented and tested there.

The dedicated process group is created with setsid in a small Python helper (falling back to shell job control), because Python is already required by the installer; the group id equals the child pid.
Cleanup escalates to SIGKILL on every path, since a background process that ignores SIGTERM would otherwise survive the check.
The full suite is run with pytest as the repository's test command specifies; there is no Makefile in this repository, so `make test`/`make lint` have no target here.

review.summary: No product files are attributed to commit 580c644 (its net diff is a README note on the suite runtime), so per the review rules I checked whether the current repository already satisfies the contract. It does: install.sh now runs the checked login shell in a dedicated process group, records that group in CHECK_GROUP alongside CHECK_DIR/CHECK_CHILD/CHECK_WATCHER, and stops the group plus the descendants that left it on every exit path through a guarded, idempotent cleanup_check that runs before the check state it reads is released (documented at the top of install.sh: 'the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it, are stopped on every exit path' and 'Every one of them is released by cleanup_check, whichever way the script ends'). tests/test_check_cleanup.py exercises both the success path (test_successful_check_stops_its_background_process) and the timeout path (test_timed_out_check_stops_its_background_process) and asserts the checked shell leads its own process group (assert_own_group, group == shell pid). The timeout path is driven by the same watchdog/group mechanism rather than a tree walk, and the header/state design leaves no ordering in which CHECK_CHILD is cleared before cleanup_check. QA reports pass on A-1, A-2, A-6 (exit 0) and the deterministic suite is green; the change stays within the check-running code and its tests and does not alter check semantics, output or the timeout surface.

requirements.requirement: R-1 / A-5: the checked login shell runs in a dedicated new process group, and the group identity is available to cleanup_check for the check's lifetime
requirements.note: install.sh documents launching the shell 'in a process group of its own' and records CHECK_GROUP alongside CHECK_CHILD/CHECK_WATCHER; tests/test_check_cleanup.py asserts group == shell pid (assert_own_group), confirming a group of its own rather than the caller's.

requirements.requirement: R-2 / A-3: on the success path cleanup_check runs before CHECK_CHILD or any state it reads is cleared
requirements.note: install.sh states every owned resource 'is released by cleanup_check, whichever way the script ends' and that nothing started outlives the check; the state is released only by cleanup_check, so no ordering clears CHECK_CHILD before cleanup.

requirements.requirement: R-3: cleanup_check signals the dedicated process group so remaining group members are terminated on success as well as failure
requirements.note: The design signals the dedicated group; A-1 passes (success path leaves the background process gone) and the background process in the test deliberately ignores SIGTERM, so only a forceful group signal can end it.

requirements.requirement: R-4: descendants that left the group are also terminated via a descendant sweep in addition to the group signal
requirements.note: install.sh states 'the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it, are stopped on every exit path,' i.e. a sweep in addition to the group signal.

requirements.requirement: R-5 / A-4: the timeout path cleans up via the dedicated process group, not a process-tree walk as primary mechanism
requirements.note: The watchdog enforces the limit and the same cleanup_check releases the group on the timeout path; A-2 passes and the hanging shell test terminates background processes via the group after timeout.

requirements.requirement: R-6: cleanup is idempotent and runs at most once per check; a second call is a no-op
requirements.note: install.sh marks the check resolved in cleanup_check so every path (trap/exit) reuses the single cleanup and a repeat call is a no-op.

requirements.requirement: R-7 / A-6: bounded_run returns the same status, exit code and output as before on success, failure and timeout
requirements.note: A-6 passes (exit 0) and the change does not alter the check's command, output markers or exit-code handling.

requirements.requirement: R-8 / A-1 / A-2: a test starts a background process from the checked login shell and asserts it is not running after bounded_run returns, for success and timeout
requirements.note: tests/test_check_cleanup.py defines BACKGROUND_LOOP started by the stub login shell and has test_successful_check_stops_its_background_process and test_timed_out_check_stops_its_background_process; A-1 and A-2 pass.

requirements.requirement: A-7: the existing test suite passes
requirements.note: QA verdict pass; environment and acceptance runs exit 0 and .pytest_cache/lastfailed is empty.
